subtype: Approach: comparing with others and feeling behind [Pitfall]
passage: Nilesh, sit down, let old Sabina tell you something. When I finished my first portfolio I was proud for exactly one day. Then I scrolled through pages from the big technical institutes. Sleek animations, dark themes, projects with hundreds of users. I looked at mine and thought, "Nobody would want to see this." I closed the tab. For four months I told nobody it existed. Meanwhile a friend who had been on the same course got an internship with a much plainer page. When she finally saw mine, she said, "This is good. Why is it hiding?" I had no answer. The work was decent. I had only compared it with the wrong people, and the cost was four months of doors I never knocked on.

qa.q: How many months did Sabina keep the portfolio secret?
qa.a: Sabina kept it secret for four months.

qa.q: What was Sabina feeling when she compared her pages with the institutes' pages?
qa.a: Sabina felt small and discouraged, deciding that nobody would want to see the page and closing the tab.

qa.q: What choice inside the story could Sabina have made at that moment, and why?
qa.a: Sabina could have shown the page to a friend or mentor, because an outside view might have shown it was decent before doubt turned into delay.

qa.q: How did Sabina's friend see the portfolio?
qa.a: The friend, who had got an internship with a plainer page, called it good and asked why it was hiding, so the friend saw the work more kindly than Sabina did.

grounding: Shows comparing one's portfolio with very polished ones, feeling behind, and delaying sharing even though the work was decent.
